feedback.problem:
A study shows how the sports preferences of young people in a certain community vary from year to year. The following table shows the results of this study. 

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Baseball** | **Basketball** | **Football** |
| To: | **Baseball** | $0.8$ | $0.2$ | $0$ |
| **Basketball** | $0.1$ | $0.6$ | $0.2$ |  |
| **Football** | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.8$ |  |

For example, $10%$ of people who used to prefer baseball now prefer football. 

Given that $1\,260$ young people were interviewed for the study and that the probabilities listed remain constant for many years, how many of those people will eventually prefer baseball?
feedback.worked_solution:
From the table, we get the corresponding stochastic matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.8 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.1 & 0.6 & 0.2 \\ 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.8\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that the matrix ${P}^{2}$ contains only positive entries. So, the matrix $P$ is regular. 
As a result, after many years, the distribution will eventually converge to the steady-state vector of $P,$ and this convergence does not depend on the initial state.

Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq=q\,⟹\,(P-I)q=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

$$
P-I=[\begin{aligned}0.8 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.1 & 0.6 & 0.2 \\ 0.1 & 0.2 & 0.8\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0.2 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.1 & -0.4 & 0.2 \\ 0.1 & 0.2 & -0.2\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix equation $(P-I)q=0$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.2 & 0.2 & 0 \\ 0.1 & -0.4 & 0.2 \\ 0.1 & 0.2 & -0.2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=-5{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=10{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=10{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.
$$

 
Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}+0{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}+\frac{2}{3}{x}_{3}+{x}_{3} & =1 \\ \frac{7}{3}{x}_{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{3}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{7} \\ \frac{2}{7} \\ \frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, after many years, $\frac{2}{7}$ of the people will prefer baseball. Therefore, the number of people who will prefer baseball is

$$
\frac{2}{7}\cdot 1\,260=360\,\text{people}.
$$
